Cauchy determinant, integer incidence-root lattice identity, and MST cut principle
correctness.rationale: For h_r(t)=r^{-1} exp(-t/r) on t>0, inner products give C_ij=1/(r_i+r_j) and contrasts G=B C B^T. Independence of exponentials makes C positive; rank B=K iff the selected K edges are a tree. All tree incidence bases generate the same integral sum-zero lattice with unimodular transforms. Cauchy determinant and rational interpolation R(z)=1-product_j((z-r_j)/(z+r_j)) imply det G=2(sum r_j) product_{i<j}(r_j-r_i)^2/product_{i,j}(r_i+r_j). The strict derivative inequalities for W(a,b) ensure each cut has uniquely minimal adjacent crossing edge; logarithmic MST exchange yields the unique normalized Gram-volume optimum. Finite-product expansion at r_j=r exp(L t_j), fixed K, proves coefficient and L^{K(K-1)}; K=1 gives 1. Independent exact-rational small-tree tests n=3,4,5 counted 3,16,125, respectively, with common determinants and strict chain optimality; no claim that finite tests prove all K.
residual_risks: Historical interpretations of D-optimal design may use a different determinant normalization; proof applies exactly to unit-norm contrasts.
